problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+{150}^{∘})=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
$$

  

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as

$$
x={720}^{∘}\cdot n,\,x=a+{720}^{∘}\cdot n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[{0}^{∘},{180}^{∘}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}+{150}^{∘} & ={150}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n, & \, & \, & \frac{x}{2}+{150}^{∘} & ={210}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & ={150}^{∘}-{150}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & \frac{x}{2} & ={210}^{∘}-{150}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ \frac{x}{2} & ={360}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & \frac{x}{2} & ={60}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ x & ={720}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & x & ={120}^{∘}+{720}^{∘}\cdot n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a={120}^{∘}.$
